content.title: How to Find the Best Hair Part For Your Face Shape
content.text: The way someone decides to part their hair is often a reflection of the times. Side-parted hairstyles were popular in the 1990s and 2000s, while younger generations on TikTok have been opting for the middle part (though the side part has been making a major comeback). Trends may come and go, but finding the hairstyle that suits you is timeless.If you aren’t sure which option to choose between a middle or side part, identifying your face shape is a good place to start. Certain parted hairstyles can enhance some features while others may mute certain angles. We’ve reached out to hair stylists for advice on how to part our hair. Keep reading for their ideas and suggestions on matching your hair part to your face shape.Meet the ExpertsMika Fowler is a hair stylist specialized in dry cuts, as well as editorial and red carpet styling.Chaz Dean is a hair stylist, colorist and the founder of WEN Hair and Body Care.Robin Emtage is a hair stylist and the founder of the hair product line Silktáge.Rogério Cavalcante is a hair stylist, colorist and the owner of The Second Floor Salon in New York City.Round Face: Deep Side PartGetty Images“If you have a round face shape, the ideal part line is down the middle or a deep side part,” Fowler says. “Both of these parts will give the illusion of length and create symmetry around your face.”Round Face: Middle PartGetty ImagesFowler warns against adding too many layers to your hairstyle if your face is round and you're not looking to play up your natural shape: “Add just enough to slim the face,” she says.Round Face: Diagonal PartGetty ImagesThe lesser known parting for round faces is a diagonal part, according to Emtage. "A diagonal part can be a good choice for a round face because it introduces a touch of asymmetry to the hairstyle, creating the illusion of a longer and more oval face shape," she says.Square Face: Middle Part with Curtain BangsGetty Images"Curtain bangs help to soften the sharpness and angular features of a square face by creating a gentle frame that draws attention to the center of the face," Emtage says. She recommends using your fingertips and a small amount of hair oil in order to shape and define your bangs.Square Face: Side PartGetty ImagesFowler says that a soft, side-swept part with either bangs or a swoop may soften the angular features of a square face. Dean recommends a deep side part to elongate your features. “The sides of the face are commonly straight, meaning an extra-deep side part is your new best friend,” he says.If your hair naturally parts down the middle, create a side part by parting your hair while wet. Then, apply some gel to hold the new part in place. Use a fine-toothed comb to direct your hair as you blow dry.Square Face: Side Part With BangsGetty ImagesFowler suggests not opting for too deep of a side part. “You don’t want to make the part too deep—this will accentuate [the angles] of a square face,” she recommends. Instead, show just enough skin on your forehead and allow your bangs to offset your angled jawline.Oval Face: Anything GoesGetty ImagesFowler says an oval face works with any kind of part. Those with an oval face can often be found playing around with any style they see fit.To find your natural part, you'll want to start with towel-dried hair. Working in sections, comb your hair back toward your crown then pull your head forward and let your hair fall naturally. Notice where it splits—this will be your hair part.Oval face: Middle PartGetty ImagesDean recommends playing with your options and mixing things up. "Deep side, middle, and side-swept all generally work well with the oval face shape," he says.Oval Face: Deep Side PartGetty Images"Oval faces are versatile and can pull off nearly any hair part, but a deep side part can further enhance this balance and pull attention to specific facial features, cheekbones, and jawline," Emtage says. "This contrast can make the face even more visually appealing by opening up one side of the face."Heart-Shaped Face: Deep Side PartGetty ImagesFowler says a deep side part will break up the chin line, which can be pointy if you have a heart-shaped face. "You want to soften your cheekbones as well," she says. "A deep side part will brush softly against your face and give this illusion," adds Dean.Heart-Shaped Face: Side Part with VolumeA side part with lots of volume and movement may give a heart-shaped face the perfect harmonious look, Cavalcante says.Heart-Shaped Face: Middle Part with LayersGetty ImagesDean also encourages experimenting with a middle part and playing around with layers to help enhance your features. "Also, try a half-up, half-down look to emphasize the eyes and shape of your face," he recommends. "Heart-shaped faces are unique, so show them off as much as you can."Diamond-Shaped Face: Middle PartGetty ImagesEmtage says that a middle part works well on a diamond-shaped face shape. "By parting the hair in the center and allowing it to fall on both sides of the face, a center part can visually broaden the appearance of the forehead, making it seem wider and frame the face," she says.Diamond-Shaped Face: Middle Part with Face-Framing StrandsGetty ImagesIf you're wearing your hair up, letting some strands frame your face can be a great addition to a middle part when you have a diamond-shape face.Diamond-Shaped Face: Side PartGetty ImagesIf you have a diamond-shaped face, a side part will help enhance your features. “A side part really complements your strong cheekbones and bone structure,” Fowler says. She adds that shorter hairstyles work best for this look since those with a diamond-shaped face tend to have smaller foreheads. Anything too long and dramatic may overshadow your face.Oblong Face: Middle PartGetty ImagesFowler suggests a middle part to add the illusion of roundness to oblong faces. Cavalcante agrees. "A middle part and long layers beautifully complement a naturally elongated face shape," he says.Oblong Face: Bangs with LayersGetty Images“Bangs also work very well for this look because they help shorten the long face shape,” Fowler says. She recommends asking for a haircut with layers to enhance your cheekbones and jawline.Oblong Face: Curly BangsGetty ImagesThose with an oblong face shape and naturally curly hair may also benefit from wearing bangs to enhance their features.Read the original article on Byrdie
